chapters.text: Apollo. To reach the Moon, predict the future.
First, estimate position and velocity at a known time. This state vector starts the calculation of where gravity takes the spacecraft.
A forward burn adds speed and raises the orbit's far side. Translunar injection sends Apollo from Earth orbit toward the Moon.
The Moon moves during flight. NASA integrated the equations of motion to target where the Moon would be.
Lunar gravity bends the path. A free-return trajectory leads back toward Earth. To stay at the Moon, Apollo needed a braking burn.
Tracking refines the prediction. Course corrections target a narrow entry corridor, bringing Apollo home.
